results.query: What target-specific tumor-localization evidence was reported for the LGR5 tracer [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 and for the Nectin4 probes in their respective preclinical models?
results.answer: Dynamic PET imaging revealed considerably higher uptake of [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 in LGR5-positive A549 xenografts (4.74 ± 0.44 %ID/mL) compared with LGR5-negative NCI-H1299 xenografts (0.98 ± 0.08 %ID/mL), demonstrating target-specific tumor localization [PMID:42000453]. The tumor-to-muscle ratio was markedly higher in the A549 xenograft model (4.07 ± 0.07) than in the NCI-H1299 model (0.77 ± 0.10), confirming selective accumulation in LGR5-positive tumors [PMID:42000453]. Biodistribution studies further confirmed that [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 can specifically target LGR5-positive tumors, exhibiting superior sensitivity and specificity for detecting LGR5 expression and effectively localizing LGR5-positive tumors [PMID:42000453]. Cellular uptake assays demonstrated markedly higher accumulation of both [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-DN96 and [18F]AlF-NOTA-DN96 in MC38-Nectin4 cells (Nectin4-positive) compared with MC38 cells (Nectin4-negative) [PMID:41916034]. Biodistribution studies and PET imaging revealed pronounced and specific tracer accumulation in MC38-Nectin4 tumor models, whereas uptake in MC38 tumors remained substantially lower [PMID:41916034]. The tumor-to-muscle ratio increased progressively over time and reached its maximum at 120 minutes post-injection, indicating specific and time-dependent tracer accumulation in Nectin4-positive tumors [PMID:41916034]. Tumor uptake of [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-DN96 was consistently higher than that of [18F]AlF-NOTA-DN96 across all tumor models examined, demonstrating superior target specificity for the 68Ga-labeled probe [PMID:41916034]. results.answer: In the multicenter study of 241 hemodialysis patients, higher arteriovenous access flow (measured as brachial artery flow volume) was significantly associated with increased left ventricular mass index (LVMI), with a mean difference of 22.83 (95% CI: 0.37 to 45.29) [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "Higher FV was significantly associated with increased LVMI (mean difference = 22.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046), whereas dialysis vintage was not (mean difference = 0.51; 95% CI: -0.41 to 1.45; p = 0.27)." [PMID:41644509]. The association between higher AV-access flow and increased LVMI reached statistical significance (p = 0.046) [PMID:41644509]. The study design was a multicenter cross-sectional study, which measures exposure and outcome simultaneously and therefore cannot establish that lowering AV-access flow would improve cardiac outcomes; cross-sectional associations cannot determine temporal sequence or causal direction [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "In this multicenter cross-sectional study, we enrolled hemodialysis patients who had undergone both transthoracic echocardiography and measurement of AV access flow, between April 2014 and January 2024." [PMID:41644509].

results.answer: In the retrospective vacuum-assisted-birth cohort of 3455 vaginal births (365 AVB and 3090 spontaneous vaginal births), multivariable logistic regression identified five factors positively associated with assisted vaginal birth and one inversely associated factor: maternal age (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07), mode of conception (OR 1.58, 95% CI: 1.07-2.33), epidural analgesia (OR 6.25, 95% CI: 3.05-12.80), gestational age (OR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.31-1.67), and newborn male sex (OR 1.35, 95% CI: 1.06-1.73) were positively associated, whereas parity (OR 0.20, 95% CI: 0.14-0.29) was inversely associated with AVB [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low-pelvic vacuum applications were associated with greater maternal blood loss (p < 0.01), a higher episiotomy rate (95.5% vs  88.2%, p = 0.03), and increased ultrasound use during delivery (62.4% vs 23.5%, p < 0.01) [PMID:42036403].
